questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Dormant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Dormant
questions.solution:
"Dormant" means temporarily inactive or in a state of suspension, like a deep sleep.

a) Sleeping - means being in a state of sleep. This is a synonym for "dormant".

b) Active - means engaging in action or operation; moving or working. This is the direct opposite of being inactive, making "active" the correct antonym.

c) Lazy - means unwilling to work or use energy. While a lazy person might be dormant, this describes a character trait, not a state of being, and is not an opposite.

d) Hidden - means kept out of sight. Something dormant might be hidden, but this word does not relate to its state of activity.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. The philosopher's theories were so abstruse that few people could claim to understand them fully.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The philosopher's theories were so abstruse that few people could claim to understand them fully.
questions.solution:
The underlined word is "abstruse," which means difficult to understand; obscure. We need the opposite meaning, which would be easy to understand.

b) Simple - means easily understood or done; presenting no difficulty. This is the opposite of "abstruse."

a) Obscure - means not discovered or known about; uncertain. This is a synonym of "abstruse."

c) Abstract - means existing in thought or as an idea but not having a physical existence. While abstruse ideas are often abstract, it is not an antonym.

d) Recondite - means little known; abstruse. This is a synonym of "abstruse."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. His shallow and _________ (ERUDITE) comments clearly revealed that he had not read the book at all.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

His shallow and _________ (ERUDITE) comments clearly revealed that he had not read the book at all.
questions.solution:
The word in brackets is "erudite," which means having or showing great knowledge or learning. We are looking for an antonym that means lacking knowledge.

b) Ignorant - means lacking knowledge or awareness in general; uneducated. This is the direct opposite of "erudite."

a) Learned - is a direct synonym for "erudite."

c) Intelligent - means having the ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills. While an erudite person is intelligent, this is not an antonym.

d) Educated - is a synonym for "erudite."

The complete sentence is: His shallow and ignorant comments clearly revealed that he had not read the book at all.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The manager was deeply _________ (COMPLACENT) with the team's very poor quarterly performance report.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

The manager was deeply _________ (COMPLACENT) with the team's very poor quarterly performance report.
questions.solution:
The word in brackets is "complacent," which means showing smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements. We are looking for an antonym that means not pleased or happy.

b) Dissatisfied - means not pleased or happy with a situation or outcome. This is the opposite of "complacent."

a) Smug - having or showing an excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements.

c) Satisfied - contented; pleased.

d) Complete - means having all the necessary or appropriate parts. This is an unrelated word.

The complete sentence is: The manager was deeply dissatisfied with the team's very poor quarterly performance report.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'ambiguity'. The contract was written with remarkable clarity to ensure that all parties fully understood their respective duties and financial obligations.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'ambiguity'.

The contract was written with remarkable clarity to ensure that all parties fully understood their respective duties and financial obligations.
questions.solution:
"Ambiguity" is the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; inexactness. We are looking for its opposite.

a) fully - is an adverb meaning completely. It is not an antonym.

b) clarity - means the quality of being coherent and intelligible; the quality of being easy to see or hear. This is the direct opposite of "ambiguity."

c) remarkable - means worthy of attention. It is unrelated.

d) respective - means belonging or relating separately to each of two or more people or things. It is unrelated in meaning.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Meticulous
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Meticulous
questions.solution:
"Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

a) Careful - means making sure of avoiding potential danger or errors. This is a synonym for "meticulous".

b) Precise - means marked by exactness and accuracy. This is also a synonym for "meticulous".

c) Careless - means not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoiding errors. This is the direct opposite of being careful and attentive to detail, making "careless" the correct antonym.

d) Thorough - means complete with regard to every detail. This is another synonym for "meticulous".

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. The speaker began to extol the virtues of hard work and dedication to the young graduates.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The speaker began to extol the virtues of hard work and dedication to the young graduates.
questions.solution:
The underlined word is "extol," which means to praise enthusiastically. We need the opposite meaning, which would be to criticize or express strong disapproval.

c) Condemn - means to express complete disapproval of, typically in public. This is the opposite of "extol."

a) Praise - means to express warm approval or admiration of. This is a synonym of "extol."

b) Exalt - means to hold someone or something in very high regard. This is a synonym of "extol."

d) Exhale - means to breathe out. This is an unrelated word.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The intern's _________ (FASTIDIOUS) work on the final report was full of careless errors and typos.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

The intern's _________ (FASTIDIOUS) work on the final report was full of careless errors and typos.
questions.solution:
The word in brackets is "fastidious," which means very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail. We need an antonym that means careless or messy.

d) Sloppy - means careless and unsystematic; excessively casual. This is the direct opposite of "fastidious."

a) Meticulous - means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. This is a synonym for "fastidious."

b) Finicky - means fussy about one's needs or requirements. This is a synonym for "fastidious."

c) Fussy - means too concerned with minor details or requirements, often to the point of being difficult to please or overly demanding. This is also a synonym for "fastidious."

The complete sentence is: The intern's sloppy work on the final report was full of careless errors and typos.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The security guard was fired for being _________ (DILIGENT) and sleeping during his night shift.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

The security guard was fired for being _________ (DILIGENT) and sleeping during his night shift.
questions.solution:
The word in brackets is "diligent," which means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties. We need an antonym that means failing to take proper care.

d) Negligent - means failing to take proper care over something. This is the direct opposite of "diligent."

a) Assiduous - means showing great care and perseverance. This is a synonym for "diligent."

b) Careful - is also a synonym for "diligent."

c) Different - means not the same as another or each other. This is an unrelated word.

The complete sentence is: The security guard was fired for being negligent and sleeping during his night shift.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'sanguine'. After hearing the disappointing news, his usually cheerful demeanor vanished, replaced by a morose silence that worried his close family members.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'sanguine'.

After hearing the disappointing news, his usually cheerful demeanor vanished, replaced by a morose silence that worried his close family members.
questions.solution:
"Sanguine" means optimistic or positive, especially in an apparently bad or difficult situation. We are looking for its opposite.

a) vanished - means to disappear suddenly and completely. It is unrelated in meaning.

b) cheerful - means noticeably happy and optimistic. This is a synonym for "sanguine."

c) disappointing - describes the news, not the person's temperament.

d) morose - means sullen and ill-tempered; gloomy. This is the direct opposite of "sanguine."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Inimical
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Inimical
questions.solution:
"Inimical" means tending to obstruct or harm; unfriendly or hostile.

a) Amiable - means having or displaying a friendly and pleasant manner. This is the direct opposite of being unfriendly, making "amiable" the correct antonym.

b) Hostile - means showing or feeling opposition or dislike; unfriendly. This is a synonym for "inimical".

c) Initial - means existing or occurring at the beginning. This is an unrelated word.

d) Harmful - means causing or likely to cause harm. This is also a synonym for "inimical".

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. Her performance in the final examination was truly impeccable , earning her the top rank.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

Her performance in the final examination was truly impeccable, earning her the top rank.
questions.solution:
The underlined word is "impeccable," which means in accordance with the highest standards; faultless. We need the opposite meaning, which would be having faults or imperfections.

d) Faulty - means not working or made correctly; having defects. This is the opposite of "impeccable."

a) Flawless - means without any blemishes or imperfections. This is a synonym of "impeccable."

b) Perfect - means having all the required or desirable elements, qualities, or characteristics. This is a synonym of "impeccable."

c) Impossible - means not able to occur, exist, or be done. This is an unrelated word.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. The agent tried her best to mollify the angry customer with a sincere apology and a refund.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The agent tried her best to mollify the angry customer with a sincere apology and a refund.
questions.solution:
The underlined word is "mollify," which means to appease the anger or anxiety of someone. We need the opposite meaning, which would be to make someone very angry.

a) Infuriate - means to make someone extremely angry and impatient. This is the opposite of "mollify."

b) Appease - means to pacify someone by acceding to their demands. This is a synonym of "mollify."

c) Soothe - means to gently calm a person or their feelings. This is a synonym of "mollify."

d) Meddle - means to interfere in or busy oneself unduly with something that is not one's concern. This is an unrelated word.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The judge's decision was completely _________ (IMPARTIAL), based on personal bias rather than on evidence.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

The judge's decision was completely _________ (IMPARTIAL), based on personal bias rather than on evidence.
questions.solution:
The word in brackets is "impartial," which means treating all rivals or disputants equally; fair and just. We are looking for an antonym that implies bias or unfairness.

c) Prejudiced - means having or showing a dislike or distrust that is derived from prejudice; biased. This is the direct opposite of "impartial."

a) Neutral - means not supporting either side in a conflict, disagreement, etc.; impartial. This is a synonym for "impartial."

b) Objective - means not influenced by personal feelings or opinions in considering and representing facts. This is also a synonym.

d) Important - means of great significance or value. This is an unrelated word.

The complete sentence is: The judge's decision was completely prejudiced, based on personal bias rather than on evidence.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'nebulous'. The vague plan was rejected, so the team requested a more precise set of instructions to properly follow for the project.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'nebulous'.

The vague plan was rejected, so the team requested a more precise set of instructions to properly follow for the project.
questions.solution:
"Nebulous" means in the form of a cloud or haze; hazy, unclear, or vague. We are looking for its opposite.

a) vague - means of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear character or meaning. This is a synonym for "nebulous."

b) precise - means marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail. This is the direct opposite of "nebulous."

c) project - refers to the enterprise or task. It is unrelated.

d) properly - is an adverb meaning correctly or satisfactorily. It is unrelated.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Jettison
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Jettison
questions.solution:
"Jettison" means to abandon or discard someone or something that is no longer wanted or useful.

a) Discard - means to get rid of someone or something as no longer useful or desirable. This is a synonym for "jettison".

b) Eject - means to force or throw something out in a violent or sudden way. This is a similar action to "jettison".

c) Retain - means to continue to have something; to keep possession of. This is the direct opposite of discarding or abandoning, making "retain" the correct antonym.

d) Propel - means to drive or push something forwards. This is an unrelated action.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Venerate
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Venerate
questions.solution:
"Venerate" means to regard with great respect; to revere.

a) Revere - means to feel deep respect or admiration for something. This is a direct synonym for "venerate".

b) Despise - means to feel contempt or a deep repugnance for. This is the direct opposite of holding something in high respect, making "despise" the correct antonym.

c) Ventilate - means to cause air to enter and circulate freely in a room or building. This is an unrelated word.

d) Respect - means a feeling of deep admiration for someone or something. This is a synonym for "venerate".

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. The coach's belligerent attitude towards the referee resulted in a serious penalty for the team.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The coach's belligerent attitude towards the referee resulted in a serious penalty for the team.
questions.solution:
The underlined word is "belligerent," which means hostile, aggressive, and ready to fight. We need the opposite meaning, which would be peaceful or calm.

b) Pacific - means peaceful in character or intent. This is the direct opposite of "belligerent."

a) Hostile - means showing or feeling opposition or dislike; unfriendly. This is a synonym of "belligerent."

c) Beautiful - means pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically. This is an unrelated word.

d) Aggressive - means ready or likely to attack or confront. This is a synonym of "belligerent."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'prosaic'. His writing style was anything but dull; in fact, every sentence was a scintillating example of his witty and imaginative mind.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'prosaic'.

His writing style was anything but dull; in fact, every sentence was a scintillating example of his witty and imaginative mind.
questions.solution:
"Prosaic" means having no factual or imaginative spirit; commonplace or dull. We are looking for its opposite.

a) dull - means lacking interest or excitement. This is a direct synonym for "prosaic."

b) fact - means a thing that is known or proved to be true. It is unrelated.

c) scintillating - means sparkling or shining brightly; brilliantly and excitingly clever or skillful. This is the direct opposite of "prosaic."

d) witty - means showing or characterized by quick and inventive verbal humor. While it is a positive trait, "scintillating" is the more direct and stronger opposite of dull.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'discord'. The team played with incredible harmony, and their performance was a testament to the many long hours they spent in practice.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'discord'.

The team played with incredible harmony, and their performance was a testament to the many long hours they spent in practice.
questions.solution:
"Discord" means disagreement between people or a lack of harmony between notes sounding together. We are looking for its opposite.

a) incredible - means difficult to believe; extraordinary. It is unrelated.

b) harmony - means the quality of forming a pleasing and consistent whole; agreement. This is the direct opposite of "discord."

c) testament - means something that serves as a sign or evidence of a specified fact, event, or quality. It is unrelated.

d) long - refers to the duration of the hours and is unrelated.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
